note: crate root
S3 request kinds and price classes; the shell's MeteredBlobStore counts requests but has no price model

request counting split by S3 request kind, with the Java's byte and error counters (bytes written counted on commit, not per attempt); its per-thread attribution (ObjectStores.ATTRIBUTION) is not ported yet

the BlobContainer operations MeteredBlobStore counts: readBlob whole/ranged, writeBlob, writeBlob failIfAlreadyExists, blobExists, deleteBlobsIgnoringIfNotExists (delete, and delete_many in batches of 1,000), bounded listBlobsByPrefix, validateKey (unmetered, S3 rule by default); blocking, caller buffers (ADR 0004, 0005)
the InputStream bodies readBlob returns and writeBlob takes, as a sink and a source over caller buffers
S3 failure kinds as one enum; the Java throws IOException subclasses
in-process stand-in for the shell test kit's metered stores (FsBlobStore under MeteredBlobStore), with S3 semantics
seeded latency, failure and throttle injection; the Java test kit does this through system properties (tests.serverless.meter.latency)
bodies through the node buffer pool, Busy when it is empty; the Java shell streams through Netty's pooled allocator with no per-node bound

the S3 BlobStore: readBlob whole/ranged, writeBlob, writeBlobConditionally with If-None-Match: * (a refused retry checked by one HEAD of the writer token), blobExists, delete, one bounded listing page; over ureq with our own SigV4 and retries instead of the AWS SDK (ADR 0005), path-style only; S3RetryingInputStream's mid-body resume is not ported (no ETag to pin the version)

one attempt of each request; isConditionFailure's mapping (412 or 409 PreconditionFailed is a refused conditional write, any other 409 is retried, 404 to If-Match is refused); If-Match on PUT and DELETE, ETags from GET, HEAD and PUT
retries with capped exponential backoff and full jitter, every attempt metered; the Java shell relies on the AWS SDK's retry strategy, which hides attempts
AWS Signature V4, checked against AWS's published test suite; the Java shell signs through the AWS SDK
streaming ListObjectsV2 page reader and error-code extraction; the Java shell parses through the AWS SDK
S3 HTTP front end over the emulator for testing the client on loopback; the Java test kit uses FsBlobStore or a RustFS container instead
the front end's SigV4 check and S3 request handling
the front end's bounded HTTP/1.1 request reading and response writing

the filesystem BlobContainer the shell runs on with serverless.store.type=fs: readBlob whole/ranged, writeBlob through a staged file renamed over the key, failIfAlreadyExists through createWhole's hard link, blobExists, delete, validateKey (the filesystem key rule); staged files in the reserved lock directory rather than next to the key; one metered attempt per call as MeteredBlobStore counts it; registers in fs/register.rs
buildPath's key-to-path layout and validateKey's 255-byte component limit, resolveBlobPath's refusal of the reserved lock directory; staged-file names and IOException-to-store-error mapping
listBlobsByPrefix(prefix, startAfter, limit)'s bounded heap of the smallest names, extended across nested directories so a page is S3's flat key order
ObjectStoreSettings' serverless.store.* keys and defaults, and ObjectStores.create's refusals

the register wire format (8-byte big-endian generation, then the value), initialGeneration's random [2^32, 2^62) with bit 32 set, ABSENT_GENERATION; BlobRegisterCasResult as SwapOutcome (UNKNOWN_GENERATION as Conflict(None)); values streamed without a whole copy
knownVersions: the last generation and ETag read or written per register, 10,000 at most, oldest forgotten first

readRegister, compareAndSwapRegister (one PUT when the generation is remembered), createRegisterIfAbsent (one PUT), deleteRegisterIfUnchanged over ETags, for the emulator and the client; the generation is read with an 8-byte ranged GET where the Java reads the whole register
the emulator's PUT streaming and GET span selection
the emulator's ETags and conditional PUT and DELETE, as S3 evaluates them at commit
the front end's HEAD, PUT and DELETE with If-Match, If-None-Match: * and ETag headers
a PUT body as ureq reads it, checked against its declared length
the client's conditional PUT and DELETE and the ETag of a GET, under the register methods; a refused retry after a lost response is told apart by its writer token
read without a lock, compareAndSwap and deleteIfUnchanged under the lock, staged file in the lock directory renamed over the register and the directory synced
underLock: 64 in-process stripes by String.hashCode of the canonical path, and FileChannel.lock's whole-file POSIX record lock (fcntl, not flock) on the stripe file, LockFileEx on Windows
test support behind the emulator feature; every call is one round, as each is one request on the object stores; logs each call's kind and key for a gate's detail
the emulator's deletes: one key, one key at an ETag, and a batch of up to 1,000 keys in one attempt
deleteBlobsIgnoringIfNotExists's DeleteObjects: 1,000 keys a request with Content-MD5, quiet mode, the first <Error> fails the batch and it is retried whole
a forwarding BlobStore over one shared store, so a node's roles reach one store and one meter; the Java shares one BlobStore object
the portable listing of a prefix's children, one LIST each; the Java lists a container's children with the S3 delimiter
